placements.why: The content establishes a mandatory deployment gate with defined scope and ownership — an architectural control governing the deployment pipeline's security. No existing strata category covers this; the repo's strata starts empty and this envelope's content calls for an architectural-governance category.
placements.title: architectural controls governing how systems are deployed and secured
placements.frame: What architectural decisions and mandatory controls shape the deployment pipeline and its security posture?

placements.title: mandatory deployment gates established as direct response to prior operational failures
placements.frame: Is the deployment control here motivated by a cited prior failure, framed as the structural answer to what went wrong without it?
placements.why: src-1 establishes the signed-manifest gate with explicit causal grounding in unsigned artifacts reaching staging — 'that is the whole reason for the gate.' src-2 records the same gate as a bare requirement in the org's stock-phrase formula. Both perform the gate as a ratified mandate justified by incident history, a thematic subject future envelopes about deployment controls and their justifications will keep feeding.

placements.title: a gate's jurisdictional reach and accountability declared as settled operational facts
placements.frame: How are a mandatory control's scope and ownership asserted as authoritative declarations rather than negotiated or proposed?
placements.why: src-3 extends the gate across staging and production as a flat scope declaration; src-4 assigns ownership to Quinton Fairweather as a settled fact. Both declare the gate's jurisdictional and accountability structure as authoritative, not argued for — a thematic subject about how operational controls claim their reach and designate their owners.
